chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), who said:
The free person and the slave do not inherit (each other).
ai.seo_question: Do free people and slaves inherit from each other in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in al-Kafi, establishes the legal principle that the status of freedom (hurriyyah) acts as a barrier to mutual inheritance between a free person and a slave. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling is often discussed in the context of 'illah (effective cause), where the difference in social and legal standing prevents the transfer of wealth, a concept that was particularly relevant in early Islamic society before the widespread emancipation of slaves.
